feat(mcp): answer each protocol revision in the shape it asks for (S43, ADR-068)

The surface was pinned to one revision and returned pretty JSON in a text
block, so a client could read the answer but not validate it, not cache it,
and not tell a read-only tool from a writing one.

All three published revisions were fetched and read rather than guessed at,
which changed the shape of the work: 2025-06-18 already had structured tool
output, so the gap was never the missing feature but the missing declaration,
and most of each revision's changes concern HTTP transports a stdio server
never had. What is implemented is what a stdio server owes each revision - the
discovery method, the per-request version with the specification's own error
for one we do not speak, the result-type field and the cache lifetime on list
results, and the liveness method answered to the older revisions and refused
to the newest by name.

Every tool now declares the shape of its answer and says it is a reader, and
every call returns both the text block and the structured one. The byte
ceiling bounds the text only, so the representation a client can validate
still validates - a detail the schema checker proved twice on its first run,
once for a payload field the schema had the wrong type for and once for a
workspace root that is legitimately null.
f2p: mcp: --list answers without reading stdin
mcp: 2026-07-28 is stateless, so a per-request _meta replaces the handshake
mcp: a malformed request is a request error
mcp: a notification produces no response at all
mcp: a per-request version this server does not speak is refused, by name
mcp: a real session answers on the protocol channel and nothing else
mcp: a tool that fails is a RESULT with isError, never a protocol error
mcp: an older client keeps the revision it negotiated, without being asked again
mcp: an unknown method is a protocol error, not silence
mcp: an unknown tool is a method error naming the way to discover it
mcp: an unsupported protocol version gets ours, not an echo of theirs
mcp: every command that writes is reachable only from the CLI
mcp: every supported revision completes a handshake
mcp: every tool answers, and every answer matches the schema it declared
mcp: every tool declares a usable schema
mcp: initialize answers with the protocol version and the read-only instruction
mcp: invalid JSON is answered, and the session continues
mcp: list results carry a cache lifetime from 2026-07-28 and nothing before it
mcp: no mutating command is exposed as a tool
mcp: ping answers an older client and is refused to a 2026-07-28 one
mcp: rules_why answers both directions, over a real session
mcp: server/discover advertises the revisions, the capabilities and the identity
mcp: skills_brief and `skills brief` answer the same question identically
mcp: the annotations say what the tools are
mcp: truncation is announced in the text, never silent
